parts: Lesson 16: Reading with Understanding: Stress Before Examination — Summary

Before examinations students — and also their teachers and parents — are under great stress. Adolescents must cope with their developmental tasks and with adjusting to a complex society; they worry about living up to the expectations of peers, parents and teachers. Optimal anxiety motivates; over-anxiety disables. Anxiety is contagious.
Causes of rising stress: identity crisis, career-oriented decisions, the attitude of teachers and parents, peer pressure and, above all, the inability to communicate with parents.

A good memory needs a good brain: oxygen, glucose, calcium, phosphorus and iron. Study in a well-ventilated place; eat milk, cheese, walnuts, wheat germ, green leafy vegetables, ragi and dates; breakfast is brain food; fibre-rich fruits and vegetables reduce stress, while fatty meals, sugar and acids take away calcium.

Good concentration improves memory. Learn by understanding and recalling, organise ideas logically, and master both the content and the process of answering. Anxiety and fear cause a mental block. Too much television steals reading time.

Time management is self-discipline: divide time into filled time (sleeping, bathing, eating, dressing, school) and unfilled time (about ten hours) and make a timetable for it. Sleep seven to eight hours. A positive thought is the seed of a positive result. Seek medical help for symptoms of anxiety or depression.
A. Managing time — a to-do list with tasks graded A (important), B (less important) and C (routine), mixing C tasks with A and B; realistic time for each task; a diary.
B. Taking exercise — brisk walking, swimming, jogging, aerobics; walk or cycle short distances; simple exercises for wrists and fingers even while travelling in a bus.
C. Developing hobbies — refreshing as sleep, chosen to suit one's temperament; they boost self-image and lift the mood.
D. Thinking positively — failure is never final and success is never an end; even Ramanujan and Einstein failed examinations; talk about your problems.
Read the whole passage for the main idea, then each paragraph for details; answer from the text; find words from the passage that match given meanings; choose a suitable title.
